records.source_rule: 5 Color Ejection applies only to a 5 with no prior positive clue; re-cluing a positively clued 5 signals the ordinary Finesse chain instead.
records.learning_objective: Distinguish a real prior positive clue from Chop Move's invisible information at the 5CE boundary.
records.critical_variable: Cathy's 5 already has a positive number-5 clue before Alice gives the new color clue.
records.blind_answer: Do not use 5 Color Ejection; interpret the re-clue as the Finesse chain.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The explicit re-clued-5 exception overrides the usual two-or-more-blind-plays 5CE threshold.
records.actor_direct_alternative: N/A: Bob is interpreting Alice's clue.
records.mutation: Remove the previous positive 5 clue while keeping the same multi-blind-play requirement and 5CE becomes available.
records.noise: Bob's own physical hand is masked; the current re-clue is represented by an arrow-only action while the historical 5 clue remains on Cathy.
records.timeline: pass: historical number clue and current color re-clue are visually separated

records.source_rule: Unknown Dupe Discharge is legal only when the duplicated cards are in the same person's hand; duplicating another player's card must mean something else.
records.learning_objective: Reject a UDD interpretation based on a duplicate elsewhere at the table.
records.critical_variable: The matching red 2 is in Donald's hand rather than duplicated inside Cathy's hand.
records.blind_answer: Do not interpret the clue as UDD.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Same-rank/color duplication across different hands fails the explicit same-hand UDD requirement.
records.actor_direct_alternative: N/A: Bob is interpreting the clue before reacting.
records.mutation: Move the second red 2 into Cathy's own newly clued group and the same-hand UDD condition can become satisfied.
records.noise: Bob's hidden physical cards are masked; the visible cross-hand duplicate remains the tested evidence.
records.timeline: pass: current Alice clue is the evaluation trigger
records.physical_state: pass: red-2 copy count remains within the two-copy deck limit

records.source_rule: In a multi-touch Unknown Trash Discharge only the focus is trash; Good Touch still applies to non-focused touched cards.
records.learning_objective: Have Cathy mark only the focus trash without learning the non-focused red card's exact rank.
records.critical_variable: The red clue newly touches both the focused slot 2 and a non-focused slot 3 before Bob Discharges.
records.blind_answer: Only slot 2 is trash; slot 3 remains useful with exact rank unresolved.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Marking both cards trash incorrectly imports the opposite multi-touch Trash Bluff rule; naming slot 3 as red 5 uses hidden objective identity.
records.mutation: Replace UTD with a legal multi-touch Trash Bluff and all touched cards would instead be treated as trash.
records.noise: Objective red-1/red-5 identities are hidden from Cathy; only positive red knowledge is retained.
records.leakage: pass: question and answer states use owner-knowledge red cards rather than exact hidden ranks
records.timeline: pass: Bob's Third Finesse Position play is already reflected by the yellow stack advancing to 2 and no stale current clue arrow
records.physical_state: pass: Bob's played yellow 2 leaves his hand and replacement draw preserves four-card hands

records.source_rule: After UDD the receiver discards the focus before older known trash, even when the duplicated identity is globally known.
records.learning_objective: Apply UDD focus-first synchronization over ordinary known-trash discard order.
records.critical_variable: UDD focus is slot 3 while known trash exists to its left on slot 2.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Discarding slot 2 first follows ordinary trash order but breaks the explicit UDD synchronization convention.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Cathy can discard the known trash slot 2 directly; it is the rejected alternative.
records.mutation: Remove the UDD context and ordinary known-trash order can make slot 2 the expected discard.
records.noise: The globally known duplicate premise is intentional because the rule still requires focus-first in that case.
records.leakage: pass: exact duplicate knowledge is an explicit premise Cathy is stated to have
records.timeline: pass: question is after UDD recognition and before Cathy's discard

records.source_rule: When exactly two new cards are touched by UDD and the receiver knows they are identical, the non-focused copy may be discarded to cause Trash Order Chop Move.
records.learning_objective: Recognize the explicit two-card exception to normal UDD focus-first discard order.
records.critical_variable: Exactly two newly touched cards are known to be the same duplicated card.
records.blind_answer: Cathy may discard the non-focused copy instead of the focus to cause TOCM.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: An absolute focus-first answer ignores the stated two-card identical-copy exception.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Cathy can still discard the focus normally; the question tests whether the non-focused discard is also permitted.
records.mutation: Add a third newly touched card and the special two-card certainty exception no longer applies.
records.noise: Exact red-2 knowledge is explicitly given as Cathy's deduction rather than hidden objective information.
records.physical_state: pass: exactly two red 2 copies are represented

records.source_rule: Unknown Trash Discharge is required when a normal Bluff reaction would leave a useful currently unplayable possibility and therefore fail to prove trash.
records.learning_objective: Choose Third Finesse Position rather than an ordinary Bluff reaction that would lie to Cathy.
records.critical_variable: A normal Finesse Position play would make Cathy's red card look like useful unplayable red 3 instead of proving trash.
records.blind_answer: Blind-play Third Finesse Position to signal UTD.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: First Finesse Position would create a false one-away Bluff note; Second Finesse Position would signal 5CE rather than trash.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Bob directly chooses among his Finesse positions; the first and second positions are the rejected alternatives.
records.mutation: If the touched card's empathy contained only playable, delayed-playable, or trash possibilities, a normal Trash Bluff could suffice.
records.noise: Bob's hidden physical identities are masked because only the positional reaction is knowable to him.

records.source_rule: An unclued 5 color Play Clue becomes 5 Color Ejection when the next player would need two or more blind-plays to fulfill the ordinary Finesse; Prompts do not count.
records.learning_objective: Choose Second Finesse Position at the two-blind-play threshold.
records.critical_variable: The ordinary red-5 Finesse would require two blind-plays from Bob.
records.blind_answer: Play Second Finesse Position as 5 Color Ejection.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Playing ordinary Finesse Position ignores the explicit two-or-more blind-play 5CE threshold.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Bob can play Finesse Position instead, but that is the rejected ordinary-Finesse reaction.
records.mutation: Advance red from 2 to 3 so only one blind-play is needed and the correct reaction changes back to Finesse Position.
records.noise: Bob's physical cards are masked; the question supplies the required blind-play count without hidden-card dependence.
records.timeline: pass: current color clue is shown before Bob's reaction

records.source_rule: When an unclued 5 color Play Clue requires only one blind-play, the ordinary Finesse interpretation remains and 5 Color Ejection does not apply.
records.learning_objective: Use the one-versus-two blind-play boundary to reject 5CE.

records.blind_answer: Play Finesse Position, not Second Finesse Position.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: Second Finesse Position would incorrectly invoke 5CE below its two-blind-play threshold.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Bob directly chooses between Finesse Position and Second Finesse Position.
records.mutation: Move red back to 2 so two blind-plays are needed and 5CE changes the correct action to Second Finesse Position.
records.noise: Bob's physical card identity is masked; the threshold is stated in the question.
